sentences.text: Today I will talk about a beautiful city.
This city is Athens.
Athens is the capital of Greece.
Greece is a country in Europe.
It is near the sea and has many islands.
Athens is a very old city.
It is one of the oldest cities in the world.
People lived in Athens more than 2,500 years ago.
That is a very long time.
Today, Athens is a big city.
More than three million people live there.
It is full of history, culture and sunshine.
Let's talk about some famous places in Athens.
The most famous place is the Acropolis.
It is a big hill in the city.
On the hill, there are old buildings made of stone.
One building is called the Parthenon.
It is a big temple for a Greek goddess named Athena.
Athena gave her name to the city, Athens.
From the Acropolis, you can see all of the city.
Many tourists go there every day.
They take photos and learn about ancient Greece.
Athens also has many museums.
One famous museum is the Acropolis Museum.
You can see statues, pots and things from a long time ago.
Another famous place is Syntagma Square.
It is in the center of the city.
There is a big building called the Parliament.
In front of it, there are guards and special clothes.
They stand still and change positions every hour.
You can also visit Plaka, an old area with small streets.
There are shops, cafes and houses with flowers.
It is a nice place to walk and relax.
Now let's talk about food.
Greek food is delicious.
People eat olives, cheese and bread.
They eat moussaka, a dish with meat, potatoes and eggplant.
They eat sevlaki, meat on a stick, and for dessert, people eat baklava, a sweet pastry with nuts and honey.
In Athens, people like to drink coffee.
You can see many cafes with people sitting outside.
Athens has hot summers and mild winters.
In summer, the sun shines almost every day.
Many people visit Athens in spring and summer.
Athens is close to the sea.
You can take a bus or tram to go to the beach.
Many people swim and relax near the water.
In Athens, people speak Greek, but many people also speak English, especially in hotels, restaurants and museums.
People are friendly and happy to help tourists.
Athens is a city of history, sunshine and good food.
It is old and modern at the same time.
You can learn, relax and enjoy life there.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
I am Emili.
See you next time.
Bye.
Hello everyone.
Welcome to the Slow English podcast.
My name is Emili.
In this podcast, we speak slowly.
We use easy English.
We repeat words again and again.
Today we travel to Europe.
We go to Italy.
Our city today is Bologna.
Bologna is historic.
Bologna is warm.
Bologna is full of life and food.
Please relax.
Please listen slowly.
Let's begin our journey.
Part two, Italy and Europe.
Italy is a country in Europe.
It is famous all over the world.
Italy has history.
Italy has art.
Italy has food.
Many people visit Italy every year.
They come to see cities.
They come to eat Italian food.
Bologna is not the capital, but Bologna is very important.
It is a real Italian city.
Part three, where is Bologna?
Bologna is in the north of Italy.
It is in a region called Emilia -Romagna.
The city is not near the sea.
It is not in the mountains.
It is on flat land.
Bologna is easy to reach.
Trains come from many cities.
People travel here often.
At part four, weather and seasons, Bologna has four seasons.
In summer, it is hot.
The sun is strong.
In winter, it can be cold.
Sometimes there is fog.
Spring and autumn are nice.
The weather is soft.
People enjoy walking outside.
The seasons change slowly.
Life changes with the weather.
Part five, a very old city.
Bologna is a very old city.
People lived here long ago.
The city has Roman history.
The city has medieval history.
Old buildings are everywhere.
Old streets tell stories.
When you walk in Bologna, you walk through history.
Part six, the red city.
Bologna is called the red city.
Many buildings are red.
They are made of red bricks.
The roofs are red.
The walls are red.
When the sun shines, the city looks warm and strong.
The color gives Bologna a special feeling.
Part seven, porticoes and streets.
Bologna is famous for porticoes.
Porticoes are long covered walkways.
You can walk under them.
You are safe from sun and rain.
The porticoes are very long.
They go through the whole city.
Walking in Bologna is easy.
Walking feels calm and slow.
Part eight, Piazza Maggiore.
The heart of Bologna is Piazza Maggiore.
This is the main square.
People meet here.
People sit and talk.
People enjoy the space.
Big buildings are around the square.
Life feels open and social.
This place is very important for the city.
Part nine, the old university Bologna has a very famous university.
It is one of the oldest universities in the world.
Students come from many countries.
They study many subjects.
Young people fill the city.
They bring energy and ideas.
Because of students, Bologna feels young and alive.
Part 10, food in Bologna.
Bologna is famous for food.
People love food here.
A famous sauce is Bolognese.
It is made with meat and tomato.
People eat pasta.
People eat bread.
People eat together.
Food is part of daily life.
Meals are long and social.
Part 11, daily life in Bologna.
Daily life in Bologna is active.
People work.
People study.
In the evening, people relax.
They walk in the streets.
They sit in cafes.
Life is not too fast.
Life is not too slow.
It feels balanced.
Hello, everyone.
Welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily, your host.
Today we are traveling to a small and charming city in South America.
It is called Cuenca.
Cuenca is in Ecuador, a country in the northwest of South America.
This city is full of history, rivers, and friendly people.
Let's explore Cuenca together.
Part 2, where is Cuenca?
Cuenca is in the Andes Mountains in Southern Ecuador.
The city is surrounded by hills, rivers, and green valleys.
It is calm and peaceful, perfect for enjoying history and nature.
Part 3, history of Cuenca.
Cuenca has a long history dating back to the Inca civilization.
The Spanish built colonial houses, churches, and plazas here in the 16th century.
Walking in Cuenca is like walking through history with beautiful old buildings on every street.
Part 4, main attractions.
The main attractions include the New Cathedral, Old Cathedral, and Plaza Calderón.
You can visit museums, art galleries, and small local markets.
The city combines history, architecture, and peaceful natural surroundings.
Part 5, the city of Cuenca.
Cuenca is small but lively.
There are cafes, shops, and restaurants.
People walk in the streets, ride bicycles, or take small cars.
The city is friendly, safe, and welcoming.
Part 6, food in Cuenca.
Food in Cuenca is fresh and flavorful.
People eat potatoes, corn, meat, and local vegetables.
A popular dish is Cui, which is roasted guinea pig, traditional in the Andes.
Local sweets, fruits, and chocolate are also very popular.
Part 7, the people of Cuenca.
People in Cuenca are friendly and polite.
They speak Spanish and some speak English for tourists.
Life is calm, family is important, and traditions are respected.
People enjoy festivals, music, and cultural activities.
Part 8, culture and festivals.
Cuenca has many cultural events and festivals.
People celebrate music, dance, and traditional holidays.
Folk music, parades, and religious ceremonies are part of everyday life.
Visitors can enjoy and sometimes join the local celebrations.
Part 9, nature around Cuenca.
Cuenca is surrounded by rivers, mountains, and valleys.
You can hike, explore nature, or enjoy the beautiful views of the city.
The air is fresh and nature is close to the city.
It is perfect for walking, photography, and quiet reflection.
Part 10, travel and tourism.
Cuenca is reachable by plane, bus, or car from Quito or Guayaquil.
Tourists come to see history, architecture, and peaceful nature.
Tourism helps local people earn money and preserve traditions.
Part 11, daily life in Cuenca.
Life in Cuenca is calm and simple.
People wake up early, go to work or school, and spend time with family.
Children play in streets or plazas, and families enjoy cafes, parks, and riversides.
Life is connected to culture, nature, and community.
Part 12, why Cuenca is special.
Cuenca is not a famous city like Quito, but it is full of charm, history, and calm life.
It combines colonial architecture, natural beauty, and friendly people perfectly.
Visitors feel relaxed, inspired, and peaceful here.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily, and I hope you enjoyed this journey through Cuenca, Ecuador.
See you next time.
Goodbye for now.
Hello and welcome to Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily.
Today we will talk about Dublin, the capital city of Ireland.
Dublin is the biggest city in Ireland.
It is full of history, music, and friendly people.
We will talk about Dublin in four parts.
Nature, city, culture, and daily life.
Part one, nature.
Dublin is close to the sea.
The river Liffey runs through the city.
You can see many bridges across the river.
Dublin also has many green parks.
One of the largest parks is Phoenix Park.
It is one of the biggest city parks in Europe.
In the park, you can see deer, walk, cycle, or have a picnic.
The weather in Dublin is often rainy and cloudy, but the rain makes the city green and fresh.
In summer, it is mild and not too hot.
In winter, it is cold but not very snowy.
Part two, City Dublin is a mix of old and modern.
The city has many old buildings with beautiful design.
One famous place is Trinity College.
It is a very old university.
Inside, you can see the Book of Kells, a famous manuscript.
Another important place is Dublin Castle.
It has been used for hundreds of years for government and events.
Dublin also has modern areas with shops, cafes, and restaurants.
The streets are lively and you can often hear music from pubs and street performers.
Part three, culture.
Dublin is known for its culture.
It is home to many famous writers like James Joyce and Oscar Wilde.
You can visit museums and libraries to learn about Irish literature.
Music is everywhere in Dublin.
Traditional Irish music is played in pubs with instruments like the fiddle and the tin whistle.
People enjoy singing, clapping, and dancing to the music.
Food in Dublin is simple but tasty.
Traditional dishes include Irish stew and soda bread.
And of course, people enjoy drinking tea, which is very popular in Ireland.
Part four, daily life.
Daily life in Dublin is busy but friendly.
People go to work, school, or university.
Students from many countries live in Dublin.
The public transport includes buses, trams, and trains.
In the evenings, people like to meet friends in cafes or pubs.
They talk, listen to music, and enjoy time together.
On weekends, families go to parks, markets, or visit the seaside.
Some people also take short trips to the countryside near Dublin.
Life in Dublin is a mix of tradition and modern style.
It is a city with history, music, and warm people.
That is all for today.
Now you know about Dublin's nature, city, culture, and daily life.
It is a beautiful city with parks, history, and music.
Thank you for listening to Slow English Podcast.
I hope you learned something new today.
See you next time.
Hello and welcome to Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emilie.
Today we will talk about Dubrovnik, a beautiful city in Croatia.
Part one, introduction.
Dubrovnik is a historic city on the coast of the Adriatic Sea.
It is also called the Pearl of the Adriatic.
The city is famous for its old walls, red roofs, and blue sea.
Many tourists visit Dubrovnik every year.
Part two, Dubrovnik has a very long history.
It was an important city for trade in the Middle Ages.
The city was independent for many years and was very rich.
The old town is surrounded by stone walls that are over two kilometers long.
These walls protected the city from enemies.
Today you can walk on the walls and see amazing views of the sea and the city.
Dubrovnik is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Part three, old town and landmarks.
The old town of Dubrovnik has many beautiful places.
Stratton Street, the main street with shops and cafes.
Rector's Palace, a historic building.
Sponza Palace, a famous Gothic and Renaissance building.
Churches and fountains that show the city's history.
The streets are narrow and full of stone houses with red roofs.
It feels like walking back in time.
Part four, beaches and nature.
Dubrovnik is not only about history.
It also has beautiful beaches and clear blue water.
Popular beaches are Banja Beach and Lepad Beach.
You can swim, relax and enjoy the sun.
Near Dubrovnik there are small islands like Locrum Island.
People take a boat to visit and enjoy nature.
Part five, food in Dubrovnik.
Food is fresh and tasty.
People eat a lot of seafood like fish, mussels and squid.
A popular dish is black risotto made with cuttlefish.
Another dish is pasticata, beef cooked with wine and herbs.
Fresh fruit, olive oil and bread are also part of daily meals.
Part six, culture and fun facts.
Dubrovnik has many festivals with music, dance and theater.
The most famous one is the Dubrovnik Summer Festival with concerts and plays.
Some fun facts.
Dubrovnik was a filming location for the TV series Game of Thrones.
The city walls are some of the best preserved in the world.
The old town has no cars, only walking streets.
Part seven, weather and tourism.
Dubrovnik has a Mediterranean climate.
Summers are hot and sunny.
Winters are mild and rainy.
Tourists love to visit in the summer for beaches and festivals.
That is all for today.
Now you know many things about Dubrovnik Croatia.
It is a city of history, beaches, food and culture.
Thank you for listening to Slow English Podcast.
I hope you learned something new today.
